analysis_tasks_no_extraction.method: read the C/5 nodes of the 41/42 trees for a sector that should contain CSI; cross its funds and its posting pattern against a comparable attached centre
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.why_it_matters: it is the one orphan of size whose absence from the structure has no explanation yet
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.result: Not a programme that was never attached. The acronym CSI was REUSED: the fund centre is 2002 'Coastal Regions Small Islands', its money since 2021 is the Special Account for Capital and Strategic Investments (fund 643CSI9000, type 313), and the fund-centre text was never updated. It is a revenue collector — 99% payroll-driven postings to commitment item REVENUE, avg 79.67 — which a programmatic hierarchy of spending activities has no node for. And the deeper reason nothing is attached: the hierarchy is FROZEN — 25 set changes in the whole window, none on fund centres.

analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: Three measurements say the organisational roll-up is configured but inert: the fund-centre hierarchy has had zero maintenance in the observable window, no custom programme we hold reads its set class, and 20.6% of FM lines post outside it. Before proposing any repair, establish what actually produces organisational totals today — a standard FM report, a BI extract, a spreadsheet — because repairing an unread structure changes nothing.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.method: look for standard FM reporting (FMEQ/FMRP_*) and BI extraction on FISTL in the execution log via A8, rather than assuming the custom corpus is the whole story
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.why_it_matters: it decides whether the hierarchy is a defect to fix or a remnant to retire, and those have opposite costs
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.result: No organisational roll-up exists. FMHICTR (fund-centre hierarchy) is EMPTY while FMHICI (commitment item) and FMHIVARNT carry data. The standard FM reporting layer is heavily used (RFFMEPGAX 441 users) but aggregates on what is spent, not on who spends it. So the orphan fund centres distort nothing — the dimension is simply not reported on.

analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: Three times now a dimension exists in two places at once and nothing declares which is authoritative: fund scope for the budget rate (ZZFIX_RATE versus the literal 001-099 range), the organisational hierarchy (set class 0312 versus the empty FMHICTR), and the fund-to-C/5 link (native FMFINCODE.ZZOUTPUT versus the bridge ytfm_fund_c5, disagreeing on 5,626 funds). Sweep for the rest of the pattern rather than finding them one at a time, and for each pair establish which one the running reports actually read.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.method: for each custom field that duplicates a standard one, compare population and then grep which is read by the executed programs from the audit log
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.why_it_matters: a future design that picks the wrong carrier inherits a silent disagreement, and this installation has at least three of them

analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: Measure what the budget rate actually did, INSIDE the standard tables, since there is no shadow to diff. For FM lines that fall inside the eight-dimension perimeter — ledger 9A, company UNES, FM area UNES, business area GEF, currency EUR, commitment item excluding GAINS and REVENUE, transaction excluding HRM1/HRM2/HRP1, fund type among the 14 flagged ZZFIX_RATE — compare the rate implied by the posted amounts against the standard rate for the same date. The difference is the mechanism's effect.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.method: select fmifiit_full on the perimeter, derive the implied rate per line from the transaction and local amounts, and compare with TCURR for the posting date
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.why_it_matters: every statement we hold about the budget rate is still about design. This is the only route left to its effect, now that the shadow-ledger route is known not to exist
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.result: the perimeter is measured and the record table covers it at 99.8% in 2025. What is still not measured is the AMOUNT effect — ZFKBTR against what the standard rate would have given.

analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: The budget rate was activated from 20240101 by TVARVC and the 2024 perimeter holds 10,660 FM lines, yet YTFM_BR_FMIFIIT has ZERO rows for 2024 and its earliest processing stamp is 2025-01-13. Establish which happened: the recording table was created in 2025 and the mechanism ran unrecorded through 2024, or the mechanism did not run at all in its first declared year. Anyone reconciling 2024 needs the answer and the two cases have opposite consequences.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.method: check the creation date of YTFM_BR_FMIFIIT in TADIR and its transport, then compare 2024 posted rates inside the perimeter against TCURR for the same dates
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.why_it_matters: a year of the mechanism is either unrecorded or did not happen
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.result: the mechanism DID run in 2024, on 7.6% of the perimeter (740 of 9,737 lines), reaching 94.7% in 2025. The control table's emptiness in 2024 said nothing about it.

analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: The fixed rate is known: 1.0416667. What is not known is which field the enhancements write it to. Eliminated by measurement: the FKBTR-to-TRBTR relationship in fmifiit_full (it appears less often inside the perimeter than outside) and the EUR budget in bpja (all at rate 1.0). Remaining candidates worth testing in order: the FI document — BSEG second local currency DMBE2, which the BI extractor already reads for USD — then the commitment lines in fmioi, then the reporting layer alone, which would mean the mechanism never touches a posting at all.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.method: test DMBE2 against the fixed rate for the same documents the control table names; the 12,396 matched FM lines give an exact document list to join on
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.why_it_matters: the whole budget-rate question reduces to this. Everything else about the mechanism — perimeter, gates, defects — is known
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.result: the FM ledger, via exchange rate type EURX at 1.09529. 94.7% of the 2025 perimeter against 0.09% outside it. FI/GL stays on the standard rate by design, and the FM-minus-FI difference is the reported impact.

analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: The impact is defined as FM minus FI/GL. Both sides are now identifiable: FM lines carrying EURX inside the perimeter, and their FI counterparts through KNBELNR/KNGJAHR/KNBUZEI plus BUKRS. Compute the difference in money, by year and by fund, and reconcile it against what the constant-dollar reports state. That number is what the organisation calls the budget-rate impact.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.method: join fmifiit_full perimeter lines at EURX to bseg_union on (BUKRS, KNBELNR, KNGJAHR, KNBUZEI) and difference FKBTR against DMBTR
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.why_it_matters: everything about the mechanism is now known except the one number it exists to produce

analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: Every condition in CHECK_CONDITIONS is skipped when its parameter arrives empty, so the effective perimeter is set by the CALLER and not by the class. Enumerate the call sites — the 12 ZFIX enhancements plus the five other BR classes — and record, per call site, which of the eight parameters it supplies. That table IS the real perimeter, and it is the only way to know which postings the mechanism can reach.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.method: grep the call sites of CHECK_CONDITIONS and CONVERT_TO_CURRENCY across package YA and the enhancements, and read the actual argument list at each
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.why_it_matters: the difference between 'the class defines a perimeter' and 'each caller defines its own' is the difference between a rule and a convention
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.result: twelve moments, twelve perimeters. 7 conditions at AVC/FI/new-item, 6 at reservation/block/reduction, and ONLY the fund type at both revaluation paths — which means revaluation has no currency or business-area limit at all. The staff path gates on PERNR through a different class.

analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: In 2024 the 740 perimeter lines at EURX pair to FI lines carrying the SAME 1.09529 rate, so FM and FI agree and the impact is exactly zero — unlike 2025 and 2026 where FI runs on a moving rate. Establish why: documents entered with EURX on both legs, a year-end revaluation, or the mechanism working differently in its first partial year.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.method: compare document types and entry transactions for the 2024 pairs against the 2025 ones
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.why_it_matters: a year where the impact is structurally zero is either correct or a gap
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.result: EURX is the UN operational rate FROZEN at the start of the biennium — the operational rate itself was 1.09529 from 2024-01-15 and again from 2024-08-15. So the 2024 lines matching EURX are rate coincidence, not conversion, and their impact is exactly 0.00.

analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: Our impact figure of -1,223,730.83 USD uses only the first of the four baselines the organisation's own control implements: BSEG-DMBTR for WRTTP '54'. Extend it to the other three — the EKBE goods-receipt amount for PO reductions (WRTTP '51' / VRGNG 'RMBE' / BTART '0200'), the document's own KURSF including the negative indirect-quotation convention, and CONVERT_TO_LOCAL_CURRENCY at rate type M for everything else. Then split the population by WRTTP to see how much sits outside route 1.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.method: group the perimeter lines at EURX by WRTTP, VRGNG and BTART, then apply the matching baseline per group
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.why_it_matters: the difference between a figure for one value type and the figure the control actually produces
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.result: -4,178,499.57 USD across all routes. Route 2 turned out to have 191,181 lines system-wide, in FMIOI — the golden held that table as 13 of 69 columns, which is why it read as empty.

analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: bkpf in the golden carries BUDAT but not WWERT, the translation date SAP uses for currency conversion when it is set. 155 of the 2024 zero-impact pairs post in months when the operational rate did not equal EURX, and WWERT would settle whether they used an earlier rate date. Re-pull bkpf with all fields.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.method: load_wide_tables.py with BKPF added to the plan, partitioned by GJAHR
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.why_it_matters: it is the last unexplained residual in the 2024 reading
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.result: bkpf re-pulled with all 122 columns. 416 of 422 pairs explained by the operational rate on WWERT, the other 6 by an explicit KURSF. The 2024 residual is closed and the coincidence reading is complete.

analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: The budget rate's PERSONNEL side is computed in the HR PAYROLL SCHEMA and nothing extracted so far reaches it — the enhancements only show the seam, through YCL_FM_BR_PAYROLL_POSTING_BL and YCL_FM_BR_PBC_POSTING_BL. Read the payroll schema and its rules to find where the fixed rate is applied to staff cost, and establish whether its perimeter matches the non-personnel one or differs.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.method: read the schema and PCRs via T52C0/T52C5 and the HR schema tables, then trace how the result reaches YCL_FM_BR_PAYROLL_POSTING_BL
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.why_it_matters: half the mechanism is unmeasured, and staff cost is the largest single category of the organisation's spend
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.result: the GATE is HR feature YYCDR evaluated against PA0001, not a range. The two-step conversion (M to EUR, then EURX to USD) exists and is DEAD CODE behind IF 1 = 2. What runs is CONVERT_TO_CURRENCY_2 under WAERS='USD'. The trace table YTFM_BR_FM_POS is empty. The payroll SCHEMA itself is still unread.

analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: Feature YYCDR decides which personnel numbers are in budget-rate scope. Read its decision tree — T549B/T549D and the feature's structure — and measure how many employees it returns 'Y' for. That IS the personnel perimeter, and it is currently unknown.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.method: read the feature definition, then evaluate its fields against PA0001 in the golden
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.why_it_matters: the non-personnel perimeter is 8 declared ranges; this one is undocumented
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.result: the tree is PERSG x GSBER='GEF' x WERKS, read from the compiled feature /1PAPA/FEAT350YYCDR. Groups 1 and 2 take five euro-zone areas, group 3 drops Belgium, group M keeps France only. 2,086 of 23,747 employees in scope — 8.8%, and 2,370 of the in-scope records are FR00.

analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: The PBC budget-rate path writes its before/after trace through Y_FM_UPDATE_BR_FM_POS into YTFM_BR_FM_POS, and that table holds ZERO rows. Separate the two possible causes: the guarded branch is never reached (no PBC position in USD passing feature YYCDR), or the update task is not landing. The first is a scope fact, the second is a defect.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.method: count PBC positions by currency and cross against the feature's population
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.why_it_matters: an empty trace on a live mechanism and on a dormant one look identical
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.result: neither 'not reached' nor 'not landing'. The PAYROLL POSTING path ran six runs in JANUARY 2025 and stopped — 703 employees, 633 of them inside the YYCDR perimeter. The PBC POSITION path never wrote, because its calls are behind IF 1 = 2. Currency is not the blocker: PBC lines are USD on 1,207,981 rows.

analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: The personnel budget rate produced amounts for six payroll posting runs in January 2025 and none since. Establish whether it was switched off deliberately, failed and was abandoned, or was a pilot that never went further. The payroll schema is the place to look — the FM side only records what arrives.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.method: compare the January 2025 runs against later ones in the payroll posting log, and read the schema for a switch or a date condition
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.why_it_matters: staff cost is the largest spend category and its budget-rate valuation stopped after one month, which is either a decision or a defect
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.result: it never started. Built, piloted for one month — six runs of 6/634/1/1/1/60 employees — and never adopted. The driver program has ZERO executions in the audit window while the control report has 43. User-confirmed: no real FI postings on that model.

analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: BR for Staff is carried by 72 'Constant Dollar' wage types in country grouping UN. Establish three things: which payroll rule computes them (the schema layer does not name the mechanism, so it must be traced from the wage type backwards); whether they are configured to post, since T52EL returned nothing for MOLGA 'UN'; and what they amount to — the staff-cost equivalent of the -2,365,688.44 USD measured on the non-personnel side.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.method: trace each 9xxx wage type back through T512W processing classes and the rules that write it, then find the posting configuration for MOLGA UN
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.why_it_matters: staff cost is the largest spend category and this is the mechanism that values it at the budget rate. It is the last unmeasured half
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.result: ANSWERED, and the answer is that they are DORMANT: all 72 are configured in T512T/T512W/T52EL and ZERO of them post in 2026. The difference is carried by ONE wage type, 999S "SUM DIF Exch. rate Fluct.". Folded into AN-DORMANT-DESIGNED-CAPACITY.

analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: YR00 is the main custom driver at 122 steps and calls a chain of schemas and rules. Trace the flow: which schemas run for which payroll areas, which rules they invoke, and where the custom logic sits against the SAP standard. That is the A_PROCESS cell for payroll and it is currently PARTIAL on an inventory alone.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.method: walk T52C1 from YR00 following COPY and PIT steps, resolving rules in T52C5
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.why_it_matters: an inventory is not a process; the flow is what makes it usable

analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: Combine three streams that are each already held: the EXECUTION LOG (who ran what and when, 15.6M audit rows), the PBC output (FMRESERV change documents, 6.4M headers, and the HRM1/HRM2 commitment lines in FMIOI), and the FI DOCUMENT HEADERS (bkpf, now 122 columns including WWERT and KURSF). Joining them gives the chain from a payroll RUN to the documents it produced, with the person or channel that triggered it — which none of the three answers alone.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.method: attribute payroll posting runs from the audit log to their FI documents via BKPF creation stamps and the PBC commitment lines, in the manner of A8
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.why_it_matters: it turns 'payroll posted' into 'this run, by this actor, produced these documents' — the level at which a control or an anomaly is actionable
analysis_tasks_no_extraction._origin: user: combining the execution logs with PBC and the FI document headers is powerful
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.result: the chain is BKPF.AWKEY = PPDHD.DOCNUM (AWTYP HRPAY) backwards through PPDIX to PPOIX, which carries the wage type and the amount. Verified by arithmetic: a PPDIT line of 46.80 is 10.96 + 35.84 of PPOIX. The run-level reading of that chain is what exposed the simulations.

analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: Generalise the finding into a detector. For every change-document object, compare the TRANSACTION CODES its maintainers use. Where one user reaches an object through SE38 or a generic route while every other uses a dedicated transaction, that is a CHANNEL DIFFERENCE — and it makes the action invisible to controls built around the transaction. Two instances are already measured: A_SEFIANI on NRINTERVAL and P.IKOUNA on IDENTITY.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.method: group cdhdr_history by OBJECTCLAS and TCODE, flag users whose route differs from the modal route for that object
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.why_it_matters: it finds bypasses without needing a policy document — the population of maintainers defines the norm
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.result: built as ALGORITHM A17. Two kinds emitted: SOLE_USER_OF_A_GENERIC_ROUTE and GENERIC_ROUTE_IS_THE_NORM — the second is the stronger and the first version missed it. NRINTERVAL is the case: SE38 is the modal route among 18 maintainers.

analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: SETS and FMFCTR are changed in production and appear in ZERO transports, while T003 shows the intended pattern with zero production changes and 8,646 transport entries. Enumerate every configuration-like object with production changes and no transport history, and separate the ones that SAP does not transport by design from the ones that should have.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.method: cross cdhdr_history OBJECTCLAS against cts_objects by object type
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.why_it_matters: the hierarchies that the whole organisational roll-up depends on are in the first group
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.result: BANK 4,588 changes by 6 maintainers, ADRESSE3 3,898 by 19, COND_A 3,004 by 8, DEBI 1,874 by 15, BUPA_BUP 1,231 by 10, PROJ 1,050 by 12 — changed in P01 and never transported. Business documents excluded by volume and maintainer count.

analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: Transported table CONTENT rose tenfold from September 2025 on an unchanged transport cadence, and it is mostly the generated authorisation layer — AGR_TIMEB, USR10, USR11, UST12 — plus the HR form-scenario tables. Separate the legitimate from the avoidable: role generation properly carries its generated entries, but a tenfold rise is a change in practice, not in policy. Establish what changed in September 2025 and which of these objects could be maintained rather than moved.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.method: re-extract cts_transports WITH as4text, then group the September-2025-onward transports by text pattern and owner
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.why_it_matters: this is IT intervening in content so the process runs — the pattern the user wants reduced, now sized and dated
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.result: mostly legitimate. Of 1,894 TABU objects since 2024: HR form scenarios 492, generated authorisations 461, directory/IMG 178, HOLIDAY CALENDARS 137 in 12 transports. The tenfold rise is calendar and form maintenance for a global organisation, not IT moving master data. The tail — T552A, TVARVC, T527O at one object per transport — is where anything remains.

analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: BR for Staff is now fully described — 72 wage types, feature YYCDR over 2,086 employees, posting configuration in T52EL — but its AMOUNT has never been measured. Compute the staff-cost equivalent of the -2,365,688.44 USD measured on the non-personnel side. The payroll results live in cluster tables, which RFC does not read directly, so establish the route first.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.method: start from the posted documents: HRPAY FI documents carry 49,577 headers, and the symbolic accounts PADJ/OTHO/LANG/HOUS/TERM name the GL side
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.why_it_matters: the last unmeasured half of the mechanism, on the largest spend category
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.result: USD 20,523,434.48 and EUR 8,057,168.94 for 2026 to July, posted to dedicated 999 accounts by ONE wage type (999S) and netting to exactly zero per currency. The 72 Constant Dollar wage types are configured and DORMANT — zero of them post. SUPERSEDED by AN-PAYROLL-FI-RECONCILIATION below: this figure summed ALL payroll postings including simulations; the real posted-only 2026 impact is USD 1,982,154.59 / EUR 796,418.86 (claim #467, still netting to exactly zero). Mechanism findings (999S, dormancy) stand; only the amount was corrected.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.next_step: the account determination is now understood: the FI transaction key is the coarse bucket and the wage type picks the GL account inside it. To get the AMOUNT, join the payroll results to PPDIT so each Constant Dollar wage type's line is named, then sum. PPOIX is the missing join and it did not load — PPDIX short-dumped with TSV_TNEW_PAGE_ALLOC_FAILED, so it needs slicing by period rather than by company code

analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: PPDIT 2026 shows tens of millions on the 999 accounts while the FI extract shows hundreds of thousands. Part of that is that bseg_union holds only 536,380 rows for 2026 against ~2.2 million for a full year, but the gap is larger than the coverage shortfall explains and it is NOT rationalised here.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.method: complete the 2026 FI extract first, then reconcile PPDHD documents to their FI counterparts and measure how much of the payroll posting reaches FI at all
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.why_it_matters: it is the difference between 'the impact is 20.5M USD' and 'the impact posted to FI is something else'. Until it is measured the figure is stated on the payroll posting side only
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.result: the gap is SIMULATION RUNS. 1,828 of 2,316 runs never post to FI and the cut is per run, never partial. The real 2026 impact is USD 1,982,154.59 and EUR 796,418.86 — my earlier figure was ninefold too high. VIEW payroll_runs_posted added to the golden.

analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: a pattern is now visible three times: 72 Constant Dollar wage types configured and never posting; ZZSUBST_AUART and ZZSUBST_SPPRC built and never populated; the PBC conversion fully implemented behind IF 1 = 2. Inventory the DESIGNED-BUT-DORMANT capacity across the installation.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.why_it_matters: we are designing a future solution and these are pre-built fields and mechanisms it could use. The user asked for exactly this: identify every custom field and how it is used EVEN IF EMPTY TODAY
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.result: inventory in brain_v2/dormant_capacity.json. Five kinds. The headline is the PRPS block: 13 YYE_* fields that together form a programmatic and donor classification of the WBS element, built and holding almost nothing (max fill 0.61% of 60,292). Dormancy is the norm here.

analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: ZZSUBST_KOMOK moves a payroll line off the SUSP suspense account onto a real symbolic account, 2,627 times in 2026 across a handful of employees. WHERE that is performed is unknown: the field appears in no extracted source file and the standard indicators PPDIT-SUBST and PPDIT-BADI_SUBST are empty on all 4,046,412 rows, so the standard substitution BAdI is not what runs.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.method: find the append structure on PPOIX via DD03L/DD02L, then the where-used of that structure; or scan the payroll posting programs and their enhancements for the field name
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.why_it_matters: it is a correction path that repairs failed account determination, and we do not know what triggers it or who controls it

analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: the PRPS YYE_* block is a complete programmatic and donor classification of the WBS element that holds almost nothing. Find out WHEN it was built, by which transport, and whether anything ever filled it — the few hundred filled rows may name the pilot.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.method: the 367 rows with YYE_POC and 323 with YYE_COOP_AGENCY are the population to look at; cross them against the transport record (E070/E07T) and the change log
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.why_it_matters: we are designing a future solution and this is the single largest block of pre-built extension points found. Knowing what it was FOR decides whether to adopt it or replace it
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.result: not one dormant layer but 31 fields in THREE lifecycles: YYE_DONOR abandoned over 24 years (82%->5%), YYE_COOP_AGENCY a 2016-2020 pilot with 3 values, YYE_POC NEW and growing since 2022 (a flag 'X', one author). Ten more fields looked 100% filled because numeric fields default to zero — A18's emptiness test fixed.

analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: YYE_DONOR fell from 82% of new WBS elements in 2002 to 5% in 2026, almost monotonically. It was the practice and something replaced it. Find what — the candidate is the fund side, where FMFINCODE carries ZZOUTPUT and the C/5 link.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.why_it_matters: a 24-year migration nobody documented. The new design needs to know which carrier won and whether the old one still has to be read for history
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.result: NOTHING displaced it. FMFINCODE-SPONSOR (0.2%) and Grants Management (GRANT_NBR empty over 2.3M lines) both refuted. What happened is that MULESOFT took over WBS creation in 2024 (85%) and fills execution modality, a constant 'UNESCO', and a Core Planner workplan code — none of which is the donor. The funding-source dimension left the SAP master.

analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: YYE_POC is a flag holding 'X', empty before 2022 and growing since — 22, 19, 104, 144, 78 — filled by a single user. Something began in 2022. Find out what it marks.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.method: the 367 flagged WBS elements are a small, concrete population; look at what they share
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.why_it_matters: the only custom field on the WBS element being ADOPTED right now, which makes it the live edge of the model rather than an artefact
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.result: it marks project ROOTS (363 of 367 STUFE=1, extrabudgetary) arriving through the new Core Planner path with the COMPLETE classification block — including a properly-named donor (19 chars, 148 distinct, matching the Core Planner's list) against 8-char abbreviations elsewhere. Rollout 0%->26%->32% of new XB roots; by hand 2022-23, MULESOFT from 2024.

analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: the donor dimension is no longer carried on the SAP WBS element and no SAP object replaced it. The plausible home is the Core Planner / PPM, which is also the source of the workplan codes now arriving in YYE_BENEF1 via MULESOFT. Confirm where the funding source is actually held, and whether SAP can still answer 'who funded this'.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.method: ADR-007 applies — the PPM brain owns that data and we consume it read-only. Ask via the ecosystem manifest rather than extracting; and check what the MULESOFT interface payload carries beyond the three fields it writes
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.why_it_matters: 'who funded this project' is a question the SAP model can no longer answer from master data, and a future design has to know whether that is acceptable or a gap to close
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.result: the donor did NOT leave SAP — it left the PROJECT master. In SAP it is the CUSTOMER master (5,401 of 12,517 KNA1, 43.1%, in six donor account groups). In the Core Planner it is a first-class role (5,777 rows over 2,738 workplans). The SF-to-SAP feed goes to BW (ZGMSPNSR), never to ECC's FM — which is why FMFINCODE-SPONSOR is 0.2%.

analysis_tasks_no_extraction.task: the flagged share of new extrabudgetary project roots rose 6% -> 26% -> 32% and then stopped at 31%. Two thirds of new XB roots still arrive without the complete classification. Find what distinguishes the two thirds — a project type, a sector, an office, or a Core Planner workflow status that never completes.
analysis_tasks_no_extraction.why_it_matters: the mechanism works; the question is only coverage. Knowing what blocks the other two thirds is the difference between extending a working path and designing a new one

hypotheses_from_operator_memory.hypothesis: FUND RESERVATIONS ARE USED AS A ROLLING HOLD. The organisation reserves funds and then ADJUSTS the reservation MONTH BY MONTH specifically so the funds are never released. If true, the earmarked-funds mechanism is not a commitment instrument here — it is a budget-retention instrument, which is a different thing with different audit consequences.
hypotheses_from_operator_memory.why_it_is_credible_before_measuring: it would explain the single largest signal in the whole system: FMRESERV is the biggest change-document class at 6,415,467 headers over 2024-01..2026-03. A create-once commitment does not generate that volume. CONTINUOUS ADJUSTMENT does.
hypotheses_from_operator_memory.method: measure the change CADENCE per reservation document, not the volume. For each OBJECTID in cdhdr/cdhdr_history where OBJECTCLAS='FMRESERV': count distinct months with a change, the gap distribution between changes, and the lifetime. A rolling hold shows as many documents with a change in almost every month of their life and few final closures. Then cross to fmioi to see whether the AMOUNT moves down in step with consumption (a genuine commitment drawdown) or is topped back up (a hold).
hypotheses_from_operator_memory.data_on_hand: cdhdr 6.4M FMRESERV headers + fmioi 2,190,893 commitment lines — enough
hypotheses_from_operator_memory.connects_to: A10 found fmioi carries FONDS/FISTL/FIPEX at 100% and no MEASURE, so the reservation sits on the same two-legged address as everything else
hypotheses_from_operator_memory.source: operator recollection, s098 — to be validated, never cited as measured
hypotheses_from_operator_memory.result: RETENTION confirmed, MONTHLY refuted. Documents living >=6 months are touched in 32% of their months (median 6 changes), and lifetimes spike at 13 and 25 months — the biennium. So reservations are carried to the end of a budget period rather than consumed and closed. The naive all-documents ratio of 0.96 was an artifact of single-month lives.
hypotheses_from_operator_memory.still_open: whether the AMOUNT is drawn down or restored — the difference between a commitment and a hold. Needs per-document amounts from fmioi, or CDPOS values which are deferred by standing decision.

hypotheses_from_operator_memory.hypothesis: THE BUDGET-RATE SOLUTION HAS A SECOND, SEPARATE PATH FOR PERSONNEL, running through HR PAYROLL POSTING and BCM rather than through the main FI path.
hypotheses_from_operator_memory.why_it_is_credible_before_measuring: this is the strongest of the recollections because the code already shows its shape. YCL_FM_BR_EXCHANGE_RATE_BL has THREE gates, and CHECK_CONDITIONS_2 is explicitly the STAFF gate: it accepts EUR *and* USD (the main gate accepts EUR only) and it INCLUDES HRM1/HRM2/HRP1 — the PBC pre-commitment, PBC commitment and payroll transactions the main gate excludes. So a separate personnel path is not a guess; it is in the class. AND IT MAY BE DEAD: MR_HKONT is declared at line 57 and never populated, and an empty range makes IN false, so whenever a GL account is passed that gate fails always.
hypotheses_from_operator_memory.method: AN-BR-HKONT-EMPTY-RANGE first — establish whether callers pass IV_HKONT. If they do, the personnel BR path is closed on that condition and staff amounts were never converted. Then trace the payroll-posting side: which document types reach FI from HRM1/HRM2/HRP1 and at which rate they were valued.
hypotheses_from_operator_memory.data_on_hand: the class is read from P01; the 12 ZFIX enhancements are NOT — EXT-ENHO-SOURCE is blocked, and the enhancements are where the steps live
hypotheses_from_operator_memory.source: operator recollection, s098 — to be validated, never cited as measured

hypotheses_from_operator_memory.hypothesis: THE BUDGET-RATE CUSTOM IS NOT ONE CONVERSION — it is MULTIPLE STEPS applied at different points along the budget cycle, and FUND RESERVATION is one of those points.
hypotheses_from_operator_memory.why_it_is_credible_before_measuring: the family is 18 objects (5 classes, 1 composite ENHC, 12 ENHO) hooked at different places, which is the shape of a multi-step mechanism rather than a single exit. And CHECK_CONDITIONS_3 is the DELETION complement used during RFFMREPO reconstruction — evidence that the mechanism participates in rebuild, not only in posting.
hypotheses_from_operator_memory.method: map each of the 12 enhancements to its hook point and order them along the cycle: budget entry -> reservation -> commitment -> actual -> reconstruction. Requires the ENHO sources, which is EXT-ENHO-SOURCE. Until then the step order is inferred from the enhancement NAMES and their spots, and must be labelled INFERRED.

The FM ledger posts on Fund x Fund Centre only, so PS never appears in FM and the two are joined by an identifier convention. Cost recovery is fund FUNCTION 3 with its own fund families and TYPE 311. And the workplan-to-SAP seam runs at 1.8 days median while human validation runs at 20.9 — so the flow is one pipeline with one slow human stage, not separate systems.

One table, one row per workplan, every hop labelled with the carrier that made it. That single artefact IS the claim.
